theory.title: present perfect continuous with for and since
theory.explanation: Use have/has been + -ing for an activity that started in the past and continues now, or has a present result. Use for with a period of time and since with a starting point. Ask How long…?
theory.tip: Identifica la relación entre las ideas y la intención del hablante antes de escoger la estructura.

content.passage: Rosa and Kim have been friends since they met at university. They have been living in different countries for three years, but they have been keeping in touch regularly. They usually send voice messages during the week and have a video call at weekends. Recently, Rosa has been learning a new language, while Kim has been working on a project. They have not seen each other in person for several months, so they are planning a visit. Their friendship has remained strong because they make time for each other.

content.audioTranscript: A: Our local group is organising an event for new neighbours. B: What activities are planned? A: We asked people what they needed and offered help. B: Some people had different ideas, but everyone listened carefully. A: We will not share private details without permission. B: And if the weather is bad? A: We will use the hall. Since the first meeting, we have been sharing updates.
